Qualify an artifact pair for accelerator-renumbering.py

This is the missing preparation stage of the existing 2554/2540/1888 procedure,
not a hardware result or a substitute for its same-container restart checks.
Run it only on a reserved IQ-9075, AGX Orin or AGX Thor with maintenance-console
access, stable power and an owner-reviewed recovery route. No published OS pair
is assumed to renumber a vendor node. Unchanged numbers mean NOT QUALIFIED.
Catalog/byte-verification commands below only read files. Download commands read
the official public bucket. Device updates are explicitly identified later.

Acquire and select exact compatible artifacts

1. On the workstation, use Bash, a pinned CLI and a fresh private work directory.
   Set CLI to its actual executable, SELECTOR to the reserved board and save:
     umask 077
     QUAL_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
     "$CLI" --json device info --device "$SELECTOR" > "$QUAL_WORK/before-info.json"
     "$CLI" --json os update-status --device "$SELECTOR" > "$QUAL_WORK/before-update-status.json"
   Independently match the physical serial/asset label and console to that target.
   Record deviceType, storageMedium, osVersion, updater feature, current slot,
   kernel, firmware and vendor runtime. The current image must already support
   wendyos-update and be at least 0.17.0. If it needs a reflash to cross an old
   partition layout, that is a separate install workflow with exact-drive erase
   authorization, not an OTA qualification. Prefer a board already running the
   selected old version. Do not downgrade a production board to create a test.

2. Fetch and retain the same manifest chain production manifest.go reads:
     BASE=https://storage.googleapis.com/wendyos-images-public
     curl --fail --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 --max-filesize 2097152 "$BASE/manifests/master.json" -o "$QUAL_WORK/master.json"
   Set DEVICE to the exact reported deviceType. Read its devices[DEVICE].manifest_path
   from master.json, review it as a relative path under manifests/, then set
   MANIFEST_PATH to that observed value. Do not infer a path from the board name
   or follow an alias to a different device/storage without the owner's review.
     curl --fail --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 --max-filesize 2097152 "$BASE/$MANIFEST_PATH" -o "$QUAL_WORK/device-manifest.json"
     sha256sum "$QUAL_WORK/master.json" "$QUAL_WORK/device-manifest.json"
   Save acquisition UTC, URLs and hashes. These files are mutable catalogs, so
   pin the downloaded copies and each selected immutable artifact descriptor.

3. Set STORAGE to the actual storageMedium: IQ-9075 ufs, Orin emmc or nvme,
   Thor nvme. From the checked-out CLI repository, enumerate complete OTA entries:
     python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/accelerator-renumbering.py --catalog "$QUAL_WORK/device-manifest.json" --device "$DEVICE" --storage "$STORAGE" > "$QUAL_WORK/catalog.json"
   The helper validates device_id and selects nvme_ota_update_* when published
   for NVMe, otherwise ota_update_*, exactly as the CLI resolver does. It excludes
   incomplete checksums/sizes, mutable 'latest' URLs and non-.wendy artifacts.
   It never substitutes a flashpack, raw .wic image, driver extension or a bundle
   for another board. In particular, Orin eMMC and NVMe have separate OTA rows.

4. Choose OLD_VERSION matching the board's current reported version after the
   WendyOS- display prefix, and NEW_VERSION explicitly from catalog.json. Do not
   select 'latest' implicitly. Review both release/producer records for this exact
   board/storage and the same supported OTA partition/bootloader family. Pin the
   release tags or producer commits/run URLs and kernel/vendor-driver provenance.
   Stable Builder release tags use the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH string as the
   manifest. Save their actual metadata and resolve tags in a local Builder clone:
     gh release view "$OLD_VERSION" --repo wendylabsinc/WendyOS-Builder --json tagName,targetCommitish,publishedAt,url,assets > "$QUAL_WORK/old-release.json"
     gh release view "$NEW_VERSION" --repo wendylabsinc/WendyOS-Builder --json tagName,targetCommitish,publishedAt,url,assets > "$QUAL_WORK/new-release.json"
     git -C "$BUILDER_CHECKOUT" rev-parse --verify "$OLD_VERSION^{commit}"
     git -C "$BUILDER_CHECKOUT" rev-parse --verify "$NEW_VERSION^{commit}"
   For each resolved commit, inspect its .github/device-artifacts.json board and
   storage row plus the BSP/kernel/vendor runtime recipe revisions. Save those
   outputs. If the selected release/tag or a nightly's exact producer run cannot
   be traced, obtain the publisher's provenance before an update; do not infer a
   source SHA from a mutable branch. These are read-only release/Git operations.
   Check that the unchanged qualification model image supports BOTH runtimes:
   the CUDA image/profile for the selected Jetson, or the pinned QCS9075 Qwen,
   QAIRT and HTP combination in qualcomm-npu-rehearsal.py. A newer date alone does
   not establish compatibility. The baseline and after-update inference checks
   below must confirm it with actual execution and library mappings.

   At preparation time on 2026-11-13, official manifests contained 0.20.1 and
   0.20.2 OTA descriptors for all three families, plus dated nightlies. These are
   examples of available descriptors, NOT an assertion that those versions
   renumber a node or are compatible with an uninspected board. Refresh the
   catalogs and inspect actual release records before selecting. The existing
   qualification format requires different reported OS versions; nightlies can
   share a reported WendyOS version and therefore may not qualify even when
   their artifact names differ. Never falsify to_os_version to force acceptance.

5. Copy each selected row's URL, SHA256 and byte size into a selection record.
   Set OLD_URL and NEW_URL from those exact rows. Check free disk for both OTA
   files plus recovery media and captured logs; Orin/Thor OTA files are several
   GiB each. Download to NEW paths, with bounded transfers and no automatic retry
   of a partial file. The following are downloads only:
     curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 1800 "$OLD_URL" -o "$QUAL_WORK/old.wendy.part"
     curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 1800 "$NEW_URL" -o "$QUAL_WORK/new.wendy.part"
     python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/accelerator-renumbering.py --catalog "$QUAL_WORK/device-manifest.json" --device "$DEVICE" --storage "$STORAGE" --version "$OLD_VERSION" --verify-artifact "$QUAL_WORK/old.wendy.part" > "$QUAL_WORK/old-verified.json"
     python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/accelerator-renumbering.py --catalog "$QUAL_WORK/device-manifest.json" --device "$DEVICE" --storage "$STORAGE" --version "$NEW_VERSION" --verify-artifact "$QUAL_WORK/new.wendy.part" > "$QUAL_WORK/new-verified.json"
   Only after BOTH commands succeed, rename them to old.wendy and new.wendy and
   preserve the verification records. If download/hash/size fails, retain the
   failed evidence and use a fresh file on a later attempt. Do not edit a catalog
   checksum or use a same-sized substitute. Verify the owner can recover the
   old supported image using separately pinned recovery artifacts. An OTA file
   is not automatically a USB recovery image.

Observe the first real transition

6. Pin the candidate Agent executable hash and confirm the installed process
   through /proc/<MainPID>/exe on the board. Record the current boot ID. Prepare
   an actual disposable vendor workload before changing the OS:

   NVIDIA: copy .github/ci-tests/python-onnx-gpu to a fresh private project and
   change only its wendy.json appId to a fresh sh.wendy.qualify.<nonce> ID. Keep
   source hashes and the resolved image digest. Select Dockerfile for AGX Orin
   or Dockerfile.cuda13 for AGX Thor. With PROJECT and DOCKERFILE set to those
   observed local paths/names:
     "$CLI" run --prefix "$PROJECT" --device "$SELECTOR" --dockerfile "$DOCKERFILE" --no-restart --yes
   Require exit 0, output twos from input ones, profiled Mul exclusively on
   CUDAExecutionProvider and fresh PASS output. A provider list is insufficient.

   Qualcomm: use qualcomm-npu-rehearsal.py with this same reserved board and its
   required inventory. It copies iq9-qwen from the pinned companion Git commit
   and uses unique app/volume identities. Follow only its baseline deployment,
   ready/status, infer-1, infer-2 and report steps for this qualification. Save
   two fresh answers, QNN HTP process/mappings, FastRPC fd, model hashes and image
   QAIRT/Genie/QNN hashes. No CPU fallback or production app/volume is acceptable.
   Keep its exact generated start/stop commands for the after-update observation.

   Bound each workload readiness/inference attempt to five minutes. If baseline
   compute fails, fix that independently before qualifying an OS transition.

7. On the maintenance console, inspect the disposable container's actual saved
   OCI spec with `sudo ctr --namespace default containers info "$APP_ID"`.
   Select one vendor character-device path from sh.wendy/pinned-devices, its
   linux.devices entry or NPU bind mount and corresponding cgroup allow rule.
   Record host path, container destination and exact driver-library path. For
   the live NPU service, use its process mappings. For the short-lived GPU
   fixture, use the retained OCI/CDI host library mount source and the saved
   successful CUDA execution evidence; do not claim an exited process still
   has readable mappings. Use the real namespace/address if this
   installation differs. Never choose tun/loop-control or manufacture a node.

   For the observed HOST_NODE and DRIVER_LIBRARY, capture these read-only facts:
     date -u
     cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
     cat /etc/wendyos/version.txt
     uname -a
     stat -Lc '%n %F %t:%T %a' "$HOST_NODE"
     readlink -f "$DRIVER_LIBRARY"
     sha256sum "$DRIVER_LIBRARY"
     python3 -c 'import os,stat,sys,json; s=os.stat(sys.argv[1]); assert stat.S_ISCHR(s.st_mode); print(json.dumps([os.major(s.st_rdev),os.minor(s.st_rdev)]))' "$HOST_NODE"
   The last output is the decimal pair expected by transition_record. Also save
   the loaded driver version from its actual sysfs/package/vendor runtime record
   and link it to the publisher build recipe/commit. If no driver version can be
   established, leave qualification incomplete rather than inventing a version.
   Capture the effective driver-library bytes/hash, not just the symlink name.

8. Stop only the disposable qualification app and verify its task/owner is gone.
   Preserve its container, snapshot, image and volume. For the Qualcomm HTTP
   workload, verify the saved stopped-by-user label so reboot cannot start it.
   Get the owner's authorization for this physical serial, exact new SHA256 and
   recovery route. Now perform the explicit physical OS transition:
     "$CLI" device update --device "$SELECTOR" --binary "$CANDIDATE_AGENT" --artifact-url "$NEW_URL" --yes
   Do not add --json: that mode skips OS updates and is rejected with artifact-url.
   Capture stdout/stderr and the maintenance console. Observe for at most 30
   minutes, then follow the recovery record with the owner; a CLI timeout does
   not cancel the device-side update. Do not repeat the update or cut power to
   make the timeout disappear. The board may reboot.

9. After recovery, confirm the same physical serial, expected new OS/slot/commit,
   healthy update status, boot ID and installed candidate hash. Cloud updates do
   not automatically reapply the candidate after reboot; if needed run ONLY:
     "$CLI" --json device update --device "$SELECTOR" --binary "$CANDIDATE_AGENT" --yes
   Repeat step 7 BEFORE restarting the retained workload, and save fresh device
   info/update-status. The same host path must now be a real vendor character
   device with a different decimal pair. Preserve before/after raw outputs and
   driver version/hash records. If the node is missing or unchanged, mark this
   candidate transition NOT QUALIFIED. Do not patch specs, unload/rebind modules,
   reorder boot services, chmod, mknod or replace symlinks to obtain a change.

10. Start the retained disposable app, without deployment/recreation, using the
    original explicit app ID. For NVIDIA use `device apps start "$APP_ID"`;
    Qualcomm uses the baseline generated detached start. Repeat actual compute
    with fresh output labels and inspect current library/device mappings. Require
    the same image/model to execute on the vendor accelerator. If the new OS
    requires a different model image or permission expansion, this is not a
    compatible pair for the existing same-container regression.

Create the reviewed qualification, then run the existing acceptance

11. Concatenate the chronological captured files into a new observation log or
    preserve an indexed archive and its manifest. Hash the exact observation_log
    file. Create transition.json with accelerator-renumbering.py's documented
    wendy.accelerator-transition.v1 schema, transcribing only observed values.
    Record the approving owner, UTC, exact serial/device type, reported old/new
    OS versions, old/new downloaded artifact hashes, actual driver versions and
    library hashes, unchanged host/container paths, and changed decimal pairs.
    Include selection/catalog hashes and producer compatibility evidence in the
    observation log. A manifest alone cannot populate before_device/after_device.

12. The owner must restore the reserved board to the qualified old supported
    image using the reviewed recovery route, or supply the same board already
    restored. No automatic downgrade/erase is part of this helper. Reconfirm
    source OS, boot/driver hash and old pair; preserve restoration evidence.
    If the pair cannot be reproduced, the transition is not repeatably qualified.
    Clean up only the qualification app after retaining evidence. Do not delete
    shared images/models, another app or an unapproved persistent volume.

13. Fill the existing renumbering inventory with both verified local artifact
    paths, NEW_URL, transition.json, recovery_record and freshly captured old-state
    device info. Generate a new ordinary bundle:
      python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/accelerator-renumbering.py --inventory "$INVENTORY" --output "$NEW_BUNDLE"
    It rejects unchanged numbers, wrong board/version/hash, missing observation
    evidence and invalid vendor paths. Follow its three-phase procedure in full:
    deploy ONCE on the old state, retain a stopped stale OCI spec through the
    transition, repair on restart with actual new inference, restart again and
    clean up. The first qualification observation is not a substitute for that
    repeat. Record unexpected/unrepeatable numbers as not_run, not a hardware pass.

Human-script completion means these instructions and tools are ready. Actual
vendor qualification, same-container behavior and recovery remain NOT RUN until
the owner-reviewed physical evidence exists. No artifact pair has been vouched
for by this repository or by the offline catalog tests.
